podcast.body: Grace Slick provided lead vocals for this iconic psychedelic rock song of the late 1960s, which she also wrote. "She went from providing the lead vocals of two of the most iconic psychedelic rock songs of the late 60s with Jefferson Airplane, White Rabbit, which she also wrote and somebody to love."

This song, written by Grace Slick when she was 28 years old, is explicitly about drugs, featuring lyrics like "one pill makes you larger and one pill makes you small." It was considered one of the songs on the "no-go list" for radio stations that avoided drug references, following the White House Conference for Drugs in the Radio Industry. "One pill makes you larger and one pill makes you small."
